subject: ENT
title: Tuning Fork Tests & Pure Tone Audiometry (PTA)
preview: Rinne and Weber tuning fork tests help differentiate conductive from sensorineural hearing patterns when interpreted with history and audiometry.

sections.title: Weber: lateralization
points: Conductive asymmetry often sends Weber to the poorer-hearing ear.
Sensorineural asymmetry often sends Weber to the better-hearing ear.

sections.title: Rinne: air versus bone
points: Air conduction normally exceeds bone conduction; a reversal can suggest a conductive component.
Interpret reliability according to test technique and hearing severity.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Tuning-fork tests are screening clues and can be misleading in severe or mixed losses.
Do not equate a single bedside result with a complete audiogram.

quickRevision: In unilateral conductive hearing loss, Weber sound generally lateralizes toward the affected ear.
In unilateral sensorineural loss, Weber sound generally lateralizes toward the better-hearing ear.
Rinne compares air and bone conduction on the tested side; formal audiometry confirms the degree and type of hearing loss.

quiz.question: In unilateral conductive hearing loss, Weber testing typically lateralizes to which side?
options: The eye on the same side
quiz.explanation: Affected ear. - Lateralizes to Affected (Poorer) Ear: Conductive Hearing Loss (ambient noise attenuated in diseased ear).
